web_evidence.note: Authorized Harper Perennial excerpt provides sustained participating first-person narration by the teacher and Maureen's husband. Initial descriptions of the killers are framed by this narrator.

web_evidence.title: The Hour I First Believed — Review by Eileen Zimmerman Nicol
web_evidence.note: Explicitly identifies Caelum as narrator and protagonist, describes chapter four in his childhood voice, and identifies family letters, journals, and a thesis as inserted material.

person_note: Caelum Quirk controls the novel's first-person narration. The authorized opening, independent whole-book descriptions, and supplied narrative passages agree. His childhood voice retains first person; dialogue, Augustine, and inserted historical documents do not establish autonomous alternating base narration. The main limitation is that every clipped quote was not located in full context, but no credible evidence conflicts with FIRST.
